_instructions: Players see this file in the launcher. Add each player-visible change here in the same commit: launcher changes to beta.launcher, game changes Beta now builds to beta.game. Releases move beta into a new entry (npm run update:game does it). One plain sentence for players per line, no commit hashes or PR numbers. See AGENTS.md.

launcher: Fixed turning on Super Mario Eclipse with a disc it can't patch failing only midway through setup with an MD5 error: the launcher now checks your disc when you turn Eclipse on and before it sets Eclipse up, and says plainly that Eclipse needs a full 1:1 copy of the North American disc, not a trimmed, compressed or other copy. Sunshine still plays from it.
Updating or switching between Beta and Stable no longer downloads Super Mario Eclipse's radar maps, the achievement icons or your language pack again when the new version uses the same ones.
Fixed Customize Mario in Super Mario Eclipse leaving the skin around Mario's mouth and chin its usual colour in the game: it now takes your colours, as in the preview.
Fixed updating on Windows sometimes stopping with "EPERM: operation not permitted, rename" while it backed up your saves: the backup no longer moves its folder into place once it's written.

Fixed installing Super Mario Eclipse, textures, cutscenes and language packs on Windows when the launcher or your disc is in a folder whose name has brackets or an apostrophe, like E:\[Games]: they stopped with "can't open file" and "No such file or directory".
Multiplayer with Super Mario Eclipse: your Customize Mario colours now go to the other players, and theirs show on your screen, as they already did without Eclipse.

Custom textures, under Settings → Graphics: choose Open custom textures folder and put texture packs made for Dolphin in it; their images replace the HD textures where both change the same texture, and they work with HD textures off too.
HD cutscenes no longer need HD textures: turn them on by themselves in Settings for sharper movies with the original textures.

Controls: each control on the Controls page now says what it does, like A button (jump) or Z button (map). If you had changed any keys, your whole keyboard layout stays as it was; Use classic keys, beside Reset all to defaults, brings back the old one (Space jumps, Shift dives, Q and E are L and R).
Mouse aim in Mario Cam, on by default under Settings → Gameplay: in the close-up view Y opens, the mouse turns the view and aims FLUDD, as in shooters.

Radar in Super Mario Eclipse: with Eclipse and the radar on, the launcher downloads the maps of Eclipse's own stages (about 140 MB), so its new areas have the radar and the full map too. If the download fails, the game still plays and the launcher tries again next time.

Fixed Play and Update & play doing nothing while the launcher removed old game versions after starting, which on Windows can take minutes: that now happens in the background and stops when you start something, and a file another program has open no longer keeps the rest of an old version from being removed.
Fixed Super Mario Eclipse on Windows with the Vulkan renderer building again every time you pressed Update & play, and never getting Vulkan: Eclipse builds now include it.

Tilt with the C-stick and Raw mouse input, under Settings → Gameplay. Tilt with the C-stick (off by default) makes up and down on the C-stick tilt the camera over or under Mario, as the mouse does, instead of moving it nearer or further; hold the right stick in to zoom. Turn Raw mouse input off if mouse look feels too slow, as on some laptops: the mouse then follows your system's pointer speed (Windows and Linux with X11). The game's settings menu has both too.

Sunshine's movies in Eclipse, on by default under Settings → Gameplay while Super Mario Eclipse is on: the ten movies Eclipse kept from Sunshine but made blurrier play from your own Sunshine disc instead, or as HD cutscenes when you have those on.

A Custom Game Source tag under Play now says when your game is built from a game source you chose under Settings → Manage, with its branch and commit, instead of this launcher's release; click it to change it.

Language: Português (Brasil) joins the list, a community translation made for Super Mario 3D All-Stars with all of the game's text and the menus, pause menu and Yes/No in Portuguese; its other pictures stay in Spanish. It needs a game version that plays any language pack.

Fixed controller buttons that couldn't be changed under Settings → Controls when the launcher can't see the controller, though the game can, as with some Switch Pro Controllers: choosing Change or Add now also offers a list of buttons to pick from.

Fixed downloads failing when the connection dropped or stalled partway through: the game's source ("RPC failed; curl 92 HTTP/2 stream reset", "early EOF"), the build tools, mods and Steam artwork are now tried again by themselves, and HD textures, HD cutscenes, Super Mario Eclipse, Eclipse's maps and language packs carry on from where they stopped instead of starting over or failing, also when you try again after Stop or after closing the launcher.

Customize Mario: Always wear the Shine shirt and Always wear sunglasses, each on its own. Mario wears them in the 3D view and in every stage of the game, from the start, while Use in the game is on, in Super Mario Eclipse too.

Achievements: 148 of them, from your first Shine to every Blue Coin and the trickiest challenges, unlocked as you play. A banner shows each one in the game, and the new Achievements tab lists them all by stage, with what to do for each and when you unlocked it, and marks new ones as they happen. The tab glows until you first open it; if the icons aren't downloaded yet (about 40 MB), opening it offers to download just those, then shows the page; a failed download is tried again by itself, and if it still fails the popup says why and offers Try again. They are yours whichever save you play; play after a warp, a save state, a cheat or with mods doesn't count. Not in Super Mario Eclipse. The launcher also downloads the icons before the game next starts; if that fails, the game still starts and it tries again next time.

Roomier tabs along the top: Multiplayer is now Online, Customize Mario is Mario and Saves & states is Saves, and What's new and Discord moved up beside the window's buttons, so every tab keeps its name even in a small window. What's new shows a dot while there are notes you haven't read.

Fixed Apple Silicon Macs being asked to install Rosetta once the build tools had downloaded, though the Apple Silicon build runs without it. Rosetta is only needed when Apple Silicon build is off, or for Super Mario Eclipse on older game versions.

Achievements: Super Mario Eclipse has its own 128, from every Shine and Blue Coin of its new areas to the castle's Power Stars and its trickiest challenges. With Eclipse on, the Achievements tab shows Eclipse's, kept apart from Sunshine's.
Players collide, a new switch under Host Game in the Online tab: players bump into each other and bounce off heads. You can also change it while you host, in the game's settings (Gameplay).

Save backups now include mods' save data kept beside the memory card (the card-a-mods folder), and restoring a backup puts it back with your saves, so a mod's progress always matches the saves it goes with.
Fixed Windows paths with letters outside the English alphabet, such as a Cyrillic user name, showing as ���� in the activity log's game and build messages.

Fixed Play, Update & play and save backups failing when your memory card folder is synced with Syncthing ("Memory card contains an unexpected folder: .stfolder"): Syncthing's own files, and those Finder and Windows Explorer leave behind, now stay in the folder and are left out of backups.

Back up automatically, under Saves (on by default): turn it off and the launcher no longer copies your saves to the backup folder before and after you play or before updates and cleanup. Back up saves still makes a backup whenever you ask, and restoring a backup or importing a Dolphin save still backs up your current saves first.
Setup now names the folder the build tools download to: the launcher's own data folder, not the install location you choose. The activity log says it too when they download.

Windows: when unpacking the build tools fails, the launcher now shows what Windows refused, such as "Permission denied" or a path that is too long, instead of the last files it unpacked, and says what to do: allow the build tools folder in your antivirus or Controlled folder access, move the launcher to a short folder such as C:\Games, or free up space.

Remove build tools, under Settings → Manage game on Windows: frees the few GB the build tools take once the game is built, and Play keeps working without them instead of downloading them and building the game again. The launcher downloads them again the next time it updates, rebuilds or sets up the game.

Windows: when antivirus removes or blocks one of the build tools while the game builds, such as ninja.exe or the compiler, setup now says which one and how to allow the build tools folder in your antivirus, instead of only "ninja: build stopped: subcommand failed", and the next Update & play sets up any tool it removed again.

Colour correction, under Settings → Display → Picture (off by default): Colour correction shows the game in the colours of the TVs it was made for, NTSC-M (Americas), NTSC-J (Japan, with its bluer white) or PAL (Europe), and TV gamma gives it the darker midtones those TVs had, so it looks less washed out, as Dolphin's colour correction does; Display gamma sets your display's for it. The game's settings menu has them too.

Invert FLUDD aim Y, a new switch under Settings → Gameplay beside Invert camera Y: it flips the control stick's up and down when you spray in place (R all the way, or L to walk sideways), so FLUDD can aim one way while the camera turns the other. It starts the way Invert camera Y is set, so nothing changes until you change it.

Split-screen co-op: Play co-op, under ▾ beside Play, starts the game for two players on one computer. The first player plays on the keyboard or a controller as ever; a second player presses START on another controller to join as Luigi, with their own camera and half of the screen, and holds START to leave. Plain Play never takes a second player. Choose side by side or one above the other in Settings (Display).

Fixed Vulkan quietly turning into the slower OpenGL: when a game build couldn't download what Vulkan needs, the launcher now builds it again once, says so in the activity log, and shows Drawing with OpenGL under Play, with the fix beside Renderer in Settings → Graphics. It also says when Vulkan couldn't start on your computer.

Language: Polski has the translator's revised text, written to fit the English lines' lengths, so far fewer lines run past their boxes. If you play in Polish, the launcher downloads it by itself the next time you play.
game: Co-op: a second player who tries their controller's stick before pressing Start now joins with that Start instead of opening the pause menu, and a controller seen twice (by DS4Windows, BetterJoy or Steam Input) no longer joins as player 2 when player 1 pauses.
Co-op: as a level starts, the game now says how to join even when the second controller hasn't been pressed yet, and tells you to connect a second controller when there's only one.
Fixed the game failing to build at the very last step when its folder's path has a comma in it (such as "Nintendo, SEGA").
Fixed the game crashing as you quit it on Windows (a crash report after Quit or closing the window).
Super Mario Eclipse: playing as Luigi or Il Piantissimo, they keep their own mouth instead of wearing your Customize Mario skin colour, so Mario's mouth and chin can now take your colours too.

Multiplayer: the other players no longer show up in your own Customize Mario colours when theirs can't be shown, they wear their sunglasses when they have them on, and in Super Mario Eclipse each player shows as the character they chose (Luigi, Il Piantissimo or Shadow Mario) instead of yours.
Fixed the music playing much quieter than the sound effects: it now plays at the GameCube's level, so if you turned Sound effects volume down to hear the music, you can turn it back up.

Aim with the C-stick now works while you spray in place too, not only in the close-up view Y opens: hold R all the way, or L to walk sideways, and the C-stick turns Mario and aims FLUDD up and down while the camera follows behind him. With L held, the control stick still walks him sideways, so you can move and aim at once. Turn it on under Settings → Gameplay.
Achievements: 148 achievements unlock as you play, each announced by a BADGE GET! banner with its icon, name and what you did.
HD cutscenes play with HD textures off, when the launcher has them on.

Keyboard and mouse: the default keys are now laid out for the mouse, with mouse look on. WASD moves, the mouse turns the camera, left click jumps, right click dives, Q switches the nozzle, E opens the close-up camera, middle click sprays FLUDD gently so you can spray on the move and Space sprays it fully, Left Shift ground pounds and sidesteps, Tab opens the map and Enter pauses. Controllers keep their layout.
Soft L and Soft R now press as deep as a trigger goes without clicking (95%) by default, instead of 40%; Soft press depth under Controls still changes it.
The radar and its full map work in Super Mario Eclipse's own stages, show its Shine Sprites past the first 120 as collected or not, and name its areas on the full map.
Fixed a crashed game on Windows leaving a helper running in the background that kept an old game version's files open, so they couldn't be deleted.

Mods: native mods can now decide which FLUDD nozzles Mario has (refusing or changing a nozzle switch or swap, leaving nozzle boxes out of a stage, choosing the nozzle a stage starts with), take FLUDD away or give it back, and put on or take off his aloha shirt, sunglasses and diving helmet (mod API 1.5 beta 1).

C-Stick Tilts Camera, in the settings menu (off by default): up and down on the C-stick tilts the camera over or under Mario, as the mouse does, instead of moving it nearer or further. Hold the right stick in and push it up or down to zoom.
Raw Mouse Input, in the settings menu on Windows and Linux with X11: turned off, mouse look follows your system's pointer speed and acceleration, for mice and touchpads that feel too slow with it on.

Super Mario Eclipse plays Sunshine's own copies of the ten movies it re-encoded at a lower quality (among them the trial and the credits), from your Sunshine disc or the HD cutscenes, with the sound in sync; its own and its darkened movies stay as Eclipse made them.
The game's window title, and the performance overlay, now show which version you're playing, like Super Mario Sunshine 2026.10.21.1 (f5b6846), with Super Mario Eclipse named when it's on.

Fixed LOAD SAVE STATE and SETTINGS being hidden under the life meter when you paused while hurt or under water: they now move next to the meter. With screen icons at the edges, SETTINGS also lines up with LOAD SAVE STATE at the right edge.
Super Mario Eclipse: the speedrun timer no longer shows a broken "Overclock: -2147483648" next to it; overclocking only meant something on a console or Dolphin.
Sound effects are muffled under water again, as on the GameCube: when the camera dips below the surface, Mario and everything around him sound dull until it comes back up.
Fixed Hotel Delfino rising out of the sand in Sirena Beach with no sound: its rumble plays again.
Super Mario Eclipse: choosing Score on the file select no longer crashes the game when a file has 210 or more Shines, and the total shows the right number from 200 Shines on.

Fixed the game refusing to save ("Unable to save to Memory Card in Slot A"), with auto save failing too, after you loaded a save state from before your last save: it now saves over your latest save as usual, so resetting no longer loses the Shines and blue coins you got since.

Mario can wear his Shine shirt, his sunglasses, or both in every stage, without visiting the sunglasses stand, when Customize Mario in the launcher asks for them. In Super Mario Eclipse every character wears them.

Multiplayer: you hear the players near you, their steps, jumps, ground pounds and voices, a little quieter than your own Mario, and a manhole lid in Delfino Plaza that one of them ground pounds open flips for everyone.

Mods: mod API 1.5 beta 2 lets every kind of mod react to what happens in the game, such as Mario getting hurt or healed and what hurt him, enemies and bosses defeated, Shines appearing and collected, Yoshi and Blooper rides, talks, cutscenes, music and saves.
Fixed a one-pixel line at the right and bottom edges of the screen staying bright behind the settings and save state menus.
The settings menu's Hold X Preview hint now shows your controller's button, like Square on a PlayStation controller, instead of the letter X.
Fixed a crash after about 20 minutes of play with the Vulkan renderer ("out of occlusion queries"), most often seen on Steam Deck.
The Vulkan renderer no longer keeps measuring goop after a stage stops using it, which may also fix the frame rate halving for good partway through some fights on Mac.
Paint and goop no longer slide, fade or vanish with FSR 1 or NIS upscaling, and cleaning matches what you see (OpenGL and Vulkan).
Super Mario Eclipse: fixed a crash when fighting the Tramplin' Stu in Hotel Lacrima's basement (water that could crash the game on 64-bit now behaves as it does on the GameCube).
Super Mario Eclipse: the stages in Peach's Castle play their music again after the character select (Delfino Square, Click Clock Wood, Battle Fort and the rest).
Super Mario Eclipse: FLUDD's spray breaks the Tramplin' Stu's mask in Hotel Lacrima's basement, as it does in Eclipse on a console; it takes a few seconds of spraying.

Hide HUD, under HUD in the game's pause-menu Settings, hides the counters, health and water gauge while you play; choose which parts to hide there, press H to switch them on or off, and pause to see them again.

Fixed a hidden FLUDD water gauge repeatedly playing its slide-in sound and blocking FLUDD's messages when a mod or multiplayer server hid it; mods can now hide individual parts of the HUD too (mod API 1.5 beta 3).
Paint and goop keep their rounded edges above 1x picture sharpness, instead of looking blocky.
Fixed the game failing to build on Windows when your Windows user name has letters outside the English alphabet, such as Cyrillic ("fatal error: stdlib.h: No such file or directory").

Fixed the game closing about a second after you press Play on Windows when your Windows user name has letters outside the English alphabet, such as Cyrillic, and HD textures are on ("filesystem error: Cannot convert character sequence").
Achievements in Super Mario Eclipse: its own 128 unlock as you play, each with the BADGE GET! banner.

Multiplayer: Player Collision for the host (in the settings while hosting): players bump into each other, running into someone knocks you back, and you can bounce off heads. Server mods can now run water fights, where FLUDD's water hits other players and they react the way Shadow Mario does when you spray him. The new Splash Battle server mod uses this: last player standing wins.

Mod API 1.5 beta 6 for mod makers: mods can keep their own files beside the memory card, per save file (saved, copied and erased with the file), and new events for FLUDD's trigger, the coaster start, Shine models and colours, Yoshi's egg and the episode select's Shines.

Server mods can now draw an arena's edge on the ground that players can't cross and that can close in during a round. They can also make water scarce: FLUDD stops refilling from the sea or items, the server hands out water instead (the Splash Battle's water capsules), and it can take FLUDD off players, for example in a waiting lobby.

Mod makers: a mod can now show its own screen when a file is chosen at file select (a randomizer's seed and options, say) before the game starts; mods that change where a file starts now apply their change once.

Colour correction, on the Display page of the settings menu (off by default): Colour Correction shows the colours of the TVs the game was made for (NTSC-M, NTSC-J with Japan's bluer white, or PAL), and TV Gamma the darker midtones they had, as Dolphin's colour correction does, with OpenGL and Vulkan.
Invert FLUDD Aim Y, in the game's settings menu (Gameplay) too: the control stick's up and down when you spray in place now have their own switch, and Invert Camera Y only flips the camera.
Super Mario Eclipse: the Long Jump/Crouch Button setting in Better Sunshine Movement now works as on a console, so at L you crouch, long jump and ground pound with L, and Z centres the camera.
Fixed the Rocket Nozzle launching Mario far too high, and higher the longer you held R, with Infinite FLUDD on in the cheat menu (F9): it now goes exactly as high as without the cheat.
Two more cheats in the cheat menu (F9): Infinite Air keeps Mario's air meter full under water so he can't drown, and Low Gravity (1/2 or 1/4) makes him jump higher and fall slower.
The episode select (where you pick a Shine after entering a stage) now runs at 60 or 120 fps when you play at that frame rate, instead of dropping to 30.

Fixed things that ran too fast at 60 and 120 fps playing at their normal speed again, among them the coin counter, the water tank's flash, regrowing goop, waterfall and seagull sounds, FLUDD's splashes, the Piantas' and Peach's sway, the Gatekeeper's and Petey's head turns, a 1-Up's blink, controller rumble, and the settings and save state menus' highlight and scrolling.

Split-screen co-op for two on one computer (Play co-op in the launcher): a second player joins any time during play by pressing START on another controller, and plays as Luigi beside Mario in the same level, each with their own camera and half of the screen. Enemies go after whoever is nearer. Coins, Shines and lives are shared, as in multiplayer: a life the second player loses comes off the shared count and they are back beside Mario a moment later; lost on the last one, they sit out until the next 1-Up brings them back. Keyboard and mouse plus a controller, or two controllers (GameCube adapters too), work. The second player can use the close-up view Y opens, and co-op plays in Super Mario Eclipse too.

When you choose Vulkan but the game has to draw with OpenGL, which can be much slower, it now says so at the top of the window for its first seconds and in the performance overlay, and building the game tries Vulkan's downloads three times before going without it.
Quit Game, at the bottom of the pause menu: it asks "Quit the game?" as Escape does, so you can quit with a controller too.
At 60 and 120 fps the camera now turns smoothly: the view moved in tiny steps, so scenery to the side slid and then jumped a few pixels every few frames.

Fixed a hitch every few seconds at 60 and 120 fps, when a frame came almost a whole frame late, and with the Vulkan renderer one every 1024 frames: Vulkan now saves its shader cache while you pause or a stage loads, never during play.

Mod API 1.5 beta 4 for mod makers: a new event as a stage is about to load, once its episode is chosen, lets a mod load another stage or episode instead; in multiplayer, the players follow the host there.

Mod API 1.5 beta 8 for mod makers, for first-person camera mods: mods can turn Mario, aim FLUDD where they look, and hide his head or FLUDD. Also fixed FLUDD still showing in Super Mario Eclipse while the rest of Mario was hidden.

Fixed a save state from one save file being saved over another. After an update, older states load by position only, and their progress went over whichever file was open, or over file A when loaded at the title screen, auto save included. A state now goes back to its own file. An older state loaded at the title saves over no file until you pick one at the file select.

launcher: The Multiplayer tab hosts a game for up to seven others, or fewer if you set Max players beside Host Game. When your game starts you get a short room code, already copied, and friends join with it from anywhere, with no port forwarding or firewall changes. It also shows under Play, at the top of Multiplayer and on your pause screen. Turn on List my game publicly to show your game in everyone's Public games list on Multiplayer, where anyone can join it. When you join, the host's save is kept in its own folder beside your memory card, so your own saves aren't touched. When two networks can't connect directly, the game goes through our server instead, which adds a little delay, and the activity log says so on both sides. Friends can still join with your invite code or address, and Multiplayer shows your NAT type, keeps recent hosts for one-click rejoining, and says why when a game can't be joined: for a host on another version, it shows the host's game and launcher versions beside yours. Ping, beside Join and on each public game, shows how many milliseconds the host's game takes to answer, connecting the way you would to play, and the activity log gives the ping when you join. Your Customize Mario and FLUDD colours come with you, so the other players see Mario in your colours and you see each of them in theirs. A green number on the Multiplayer tab's icon shows how many players are in public games right now. Dedicated servers that welcome players on other recent builds can be joined from Public games and with their room code, and when a host needs a newer game or launcher than yours, joining tells you which version you need.

While you host or join a game with a room code, friends can join you from Discord: invite them with the + button in a Discord chat, and they click Join on the invite to start their launcher and join your room, even if it was closed. In a public game, friends who Ask to Join on your Discord profile are let in right away; in a private one, click the notification to let them in. This needs Show on Discord turned on in Settings, and your friends need SMS Launcher installed.

Mods: a new Mods tab in Settings downloads mods from their own releases, updates them, and switches them on or off; their settings are in the game's Mods menu (F1). The first is Seamless Episodes: after a Shine Sprite is saved, the world's next episode starts right away with its opening cutscene, without going back to Delfino Plaza or through the episode select, in singleplayer or when you host multiplayer.

Renderer: choose OpenGL or Vulkan under Graphics, on Windows, Linux and Mac, Super Mario Eclipse included. Vulkan is experimental: it is often faster, and if it can't start on your computer the game uses OpenGL. On Windows, choosing Vulkan builds the game again the first time.

Apple Silicon build: on a Mac with Apple Silicon, the game and Super Mario Eclipse now build for it instead of running through Rosetta, which is faster. If yours plays through Rosetta, it switches by itself once your game version can build it, and a message says so with a Keep Rosetta button. Apple Silicon build under Manage game, Files changes it any time.

Customize Mario now paints FLUDD too: under FLUDD, pick colours for its body, metal, straps and trim, or try a FLUDD preset like Gold or Midnight. FLUDD wears them in the game and in Super Mario Eclipse, and other players see your FLUDD in your colours in multiplayer. Mario's presets leave FLUDD's colours alone.

Auto Save, on by default under Settings → Gameplay: the game saves by itself after Shine Sprites, blue coins, nozzle boxes and Yoshi instead of asking, with a Shine turning at the bottom left while it saves and the game's save sound once it has. Turn it off to get the prompts back.

Settings you change in the game's own settings menu (pause, then Y) are now kept: when the game closes the launcher saves them, so Settings shows them and the next game starts with them. Settings → Gameplay also has Music volume and Sound effects volume under Volume.

Radar: turn on a round map at the top right of the game under Gameplay. It shows the area close around Mario, with the area's Shine Sprites and blue coins, and is off by default. Open the map, a new control under Controls (M, or Back on a controller), shows the whole area.

A new layout: tabs along the top open Play, Multiplayer (marked Beta), Customize Mario, Saves & states, What's new and Settings, so the Play button has only Play and the Add to Steam banner beside it. The activity log moved to a button at the right of the status bar that opens it on any page, under the page, and a task's progress shows in the status bar too; the log now opens by itself only when something fails. Escape, or B on a controller, goes back to Play, and LB/RB step through the tabs.

What's new is easier to read: Beta and every release are listed down the left, and the one you pick shows its launcher and game changes side by side, each with a short bold headline, its fixes in a checklist, and long notes cut to a few lines that open in full when you click them.

Choosing your game disc now checks the whole file: an incomplete copy, an RVZ, WIA, GCZ or NKit image, a ZIP, 7-Zip or RAR archive, a Wii disc, or another region or game each get a message saying what it is and what to do, instead of failing partway through setting up the game. When setting up does fail, the message now gives the reason instead of only the file that failed.

Updating the game and switching between Super Mario Sunshine and Super Mario Eclipse are faster: the launcher keeps the game files it compiled and reuses every one whose code didn't change, so a build compiles only what did. It takes up to 2 GB, and Free up space under Manage game clears it.
Build tools that no installed game version uses any more are removed after the game is built, which frees a few gigabytes each time the build tools are updated.
Messages in the corner of the launcher now have a close button, and sit below the tabs so they no longer cover Settings.

Super Mario Eclipse now credits the Eclipse team: its switch in Settings says it was created by them, with a GitHub link to the mod, and while Eclipse is on, a banner on the Play page opens Super Mario Eclipse on GitHub.
The launcher has a new logo: a golden sun at the top left.
Fixed HD texture, HD cutscene and language pack downloads failing on some Windows computers with a CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED error.

changes: Multiplayer: up to eight players play the host's level and save together as Mario, Luigi, Wario, Metal Mario, and Fire, Purple, Orange and Ice Mario, each in their own colours, sharing blue and red coins, coins, lives, enemies, switches, FLUDD's water and the goop it cleans, getting every Shine and watching cutscenes together, fighting the same bosses, Bowser and Bowser Jr. on a hot tub that tips under every player, goop piranha plants and Shadow Mario, cooling off the same Chain Chomp, cleaning the same goop-covered Piantas, hitting the same switches and boxes, carrying and throwing the same fruit and barrels, popping the same balloons, riding the same boats, Ferris wheel and merry-go-round, playing the same casino slots, rolling the same watermelon, finding NPCs in the same places and stopping to talk to them, seeing the same seagulls, pigeons and fish (and the coins they carry), riding the same cranes, windmills, lifts and swinging boards, feeding Yoshi's egg the same fruit and each hatching their own Yoshi, with enemies and events reacting to whichever player is nearest, following the host to other areas, and watching the others when out of lives until a 1-up brings them back. Friends can join once the host has picked a save file, and anyone joining while the host is on the way somewhere arrives where the host is going. Everyone arrives in each level the way the host does, with the same opening and movies, and a cutscene plays once for everyone. Enemies, NPCs and Shadow Mario move smoothly in step with the host's game and chase each player where they really are, a coin two players grab at once counts once, and if the connection drops, the game reconnects by itself and you keep your character.

Multiplayer: you see the others as they really play: each player in their own Customize Mario colours and FLUDD colours (in HD with the HD textures), or their character's when they haven't customized Mario, with their name over their head while you're near them, and the fruit they carry, where they aim FLUDD, the Blooper they surf on, the effects they make and their coaster car in the fight with Mecha-Bowser. Graffiti is shared too: anyone's water cleans it for everyone, and players who join later find it as it is now. Messages and the player list use the names players joined with.

Multiplayer: the group plays through the story together. The host picks the episode while everyone watches their episode select, any player can lead the group through a pipe, a painting, a secret course's entrance or a story event, and the Shine Get lines every player up beside the one holding the Shine. Your lives counter shows when another player loses a life or gets a 1-up, every 50 coins the group collects gives one extra life, and when everyone is out of lives it's game over for all of you, back to Delfino Plaza with your lives refilled. Save prompts go to the host, a joining player's file select says those files are on the multiplayer card and not your own saves, and when the host quits or stops answering, everyone is told why and goes back to their own title screen.

Multiplayer: the game can now run as a dedicated server (sms-server) that hosts around the clock and lists itself in Public games, with game modes like the Squid Race that need nothing extra on your side.

Radar: a round map at the top right shows the area close around Mario, north up, with an arrow for the way he faces and the area's Shine Sprites and blue coins, including those still to appear. It scrolls as he moves, moves down out of the way while the life meter is showing, and hides in cutscenes and the pause menu. D-pad up zooms it in and out, and M, or Back on a controller, opens the whole area's map, with the game's own map sounds; you can keep moving while it's open.

A settings menu in the game: pause and press Y to change the launcher's graphics, display, gameplay and control settings while you play, including separate music and sound effects volume. Changes show at once (screen format, frame rate and HD texture loading from the next area), and the launcher keeps them.

Auto save: with the launcher's Auto Save on, the game saves by itself where it used to ask, and a Shine at the bottom left shows it saving. If it can't save without asking (no save file yet, or a file saved over elsewhere), the usual prompt opens instead; a game over still asks.

Mods: native mods and Lua script mods made with the SMS mod SDK go in the game's mods folder, and F1 in the game opens the Mods menu with their settings. Mods can tell why a stage is left, send the game straight to an episode and read each world's episodes, and server mods can move, add or remove the level's objects, change players' health, water and nozzle, set game rules, and show standings, markers, fades, camera shakes and rumble.
Vulkan and Apple Silicon: the game can draw with Vulkan, and on Apple Silicon Macs it and Super Mario Eclipse can run natively instead of through Rosetta.

With button prompts set to Xbox, PlayStation, Steam Deck, keyboard or Automatic, the B shown over a character you can talk to is now that controller's B button (or your key for it) instead of the GameCube B.
Super Mario Eclipse downloads its mods' sources once for every game version instead of again for each, saving about 110 MB per update and nearly 1 GB of disk space per game version.

Fixed HD textures on some surfaces, such as Delfino Plaza's tiles and the wooden piers, turning blurry a second after a level loads, or right away on later launches: they now stay as sharp up close as the texture pack makes them.
Fixed GameCube adapters that set up their own driver on Windows, such as the Lossless Adapter in its Switch/Dolphin mode, not being picked up by the game while Dolphin could use them.
Fixed Super Mario Eclipse crashing on a Mac when you quit the game.
Fixed the game freezing as it starts on some Linux computers when the sound server stopped answering: it now plays without sound after a few seconds.
Fixed Super Mario Eclipse asking to save after every Shine and blue coin in the 64-bit game, even with its Save Prompts setting on AUTO SAVE; it now saves by itself as that setting says.

launcher: Aim with the C-stick: a new switch under Camera lets the C-stick aim FLUDD in the close-up view Y opens. Off by default.

Customize Mario now works in Super Mario Eclipse too: Mario plays there in the colours you pick, and Luigi and Piantissimo keep their own look. They share Mario's mouth, so with a skin colour chosen, his mouth keeps its usual colour in Eclipse.
Pause menu tracker: turn the game's new Shine Sprite and blue coin tracker off under Gameplay if you'd rather not see it in the pause menu.
Skip intro: turn it on under Gameplay to start the game at the title screen, without the Nintendo and Dolby logos or the opening movie.

Customize Mario no longer keeps your graphics card busy while you leave it open: Mario holds still after 15 seconds untouched and while the launcher is in the background, and moves again when you point at him. On some older PCs, leaving it open made the launcher's graphics stop working.

Windows: when the launcher's folder is too deep for Windows to build the game in, as with a portable launcher kept inside another app's folder, it now says so as soon as it opens and again whenever you try to set up, update or build the game, marks how much of the path is too long and how to fix it, and stops before downloading the build tools instead of the build failing with "No such file or directory".
Mouse buttons can now be bound under Settings → Controls: choose Change or Add, then click the left, right, middle or a side mouse button, and the game reads it like a key.

Windows: fixed builds failing with "The C compiler is not able to compile a simple test program", and the game then not starting with "DLL entry point not found", on PCs where another program put older copies of DLLs like libwinpthread-1.dll or zlib1.dll in System32. The build tools and the game now always load their own copies, and the activity log says when Windows has others.

changes: Pause menu tracker: the pause menu shows how many of an area's Shine Sprites and blue coins you have, out of all there are, starting with the area you're in; L and R switch to the other areas you've been to.
Fixed Super Mario Eclipse never saving a level's coin record, so the episode select and the map always showed 00.

Fixed the game lagging for as long as the controller rumbles, seen most on Linux with Steam Input and at high frame rates. Weak rumbles now play as a gentler, steady rumble instead of quick full-strength pulses.
Widescreen: the black wipe that opens at the end of a stage's title card now covers the whole screen and slides out past its edges, instead of leaving the stage showing at both sides.
Fixed missing music in Super Mario Eclipse: the Tutorial, the castle's other floors and its basement played no song, and other stages sometimes lost theirs.
The Nintendo and Dolby logos at startup can now be skipped with A, like the opening movie.
Escape now asks "Quit the game?" before quitting, with Cancel picked to begin with, instead of closing the game straight away and losing unsaved progress.

Mouse look now orbits the camera around Mario: moving the mouse up and down tilts the camera over or under him at the same distance instead of moving it nearer and further, and the mouse wheel zooms it, scrolling down to move it out and up to bring it in. L still recentres it.
Mouse buttons can be bound to the game's buttons, as keys are, and the camera follows the mouse more closely as you turn it.
Fixed Invert camera Y not flipping FLUDD's up and down aim while you hold R all the way down to spray in place.

Aim with the C-stick: in the close-up view Y opens, the C-stick can aim FLUDD and turn the view, as in modern shooters, the same way it turns the normal camera (Invert camera X and Y apply); the control stick still works there too.

launcher: Fixed choosing a game source on Windows failing with a "Permission denied" error, and failed game downloads showing that error instead of what went wrong.

Portable launcher: copy the launcher and its SMS-Launcher-Portable folder to another drive or computer and keep playing without setting up again. It finds a disc you keep beside the launcher or in that folder, and no longer rebuilds the game or fails to start it after a move.

When a game update is ready, the ▾ beside the main button now offers Update only, to install it without starting the game, as well as Update & play and Play now. With Update automatically off, Play stays the main button and the update choices are in the ▾ menu.

Customize Mario: once you've chosen your disc, Customize Mario on the home screen shows Mario from your own disc in 3D, idling, so you can turn him around and pick colours for his cap, emblem, shirt, overalls, buttons, gloves, shoes, skin, hair, eyebrows, mustache and eyes, or try a preset like Luigi or Wario. He plays in your colours the next time the game starts, HD textures included; turn off Use in the game to keep his usual look in the game. You can also try him in the Shine shirt or with FLUDD and its nozzles in the preview.
Customize Mario still shows Mario on computers whose graphics card the launcher can't use, and if his 3D view stops, Try again or Restart launcher brings it back.

changes: Fixed a thin black line down the middle of the screen while a circle wipe opens, with widescreen on at an internal resolution above 1x.
Fixed a faint see-through square around the shadows of palm trees and awnings with HD textures on, in Delfino Plaza, Pinna Park and on the airstrip.
Fixed the game closing about two seconds after it starts on some Macs with HD textures on, with "no memory below 2 GiB for a thread stack".
Fixed the moving pictures in the plaza's level entrances, such as the Bianco Hills M, freezing on one frame and only moving now and then on computers that can't keep up the frame rate.
Mario can play in the colours you pick in the launcher's Customize Mario, with HD textures on or off.
Fixed the game sometimes crashing right after a cutscene, such as FLUDD's on the airstrip.

launcher: Rumble strength: set how hard your controller rumbles under Settings → Controls, and feel it on your controller as you move the slider. 50% matches the console; turn it up for stronger rumble, or down to 0% to turn it off.
Settings → Controls shows when a GameCube adapter is plugged in and whether the game can read it, and on Linux, Allow access gives the game permission to open it.
Fixed setup on Windows stopping with "operation not permitted" while the build tools were moved into place, usually because antivirus was still scanning them.

Fixed Super Mario Eclipse with a language other than English chosen: Eclipse now always plays in English, and Settings greys out Language while Eclipse is on. Your language comes back when you turn Eclipse off.

Import a Dolphin save now takes Super Mario Eclipse saves (04-GMSE-super_mario_sunshine.gci) and puts them in Eclipse's save. You can drop several saves, or the whole Dolphin memory card folder, at once: Eclipse's settings files and saves with no progress are skipped instead of replacing yours, and after importing, Settings → Saves shows which game each save is for and the Shines in each file.

Add to Steam keeps your other non-Steam games safer: it backs up Steam's list before closing Steam, and if Steam loses games from the list as it closes, it puts the list from before back and stops instead of adding. It also adds to the Steam account signed in most recently, even when another account on the computer was signed in before.

Fixed Add to Steam on a Steam Deck with NonSteamLaunchers installed emptying your list of non-Steam games: NonSteamLaunchers cleared the list because the launcher saved it without the permission NonSteamLaunchers checks for.
Setting up Super Mario Eclipse now shows its 900 MB download as it goes, then its unpacking and patching, instead of sitting on one line for minutes and looking stuck.

On Windows, setup now downloads the build tools again when a program the game build needs is missing (antivirus sometimes removes one), instead of failing with "unable to find a build program corresponding to Ninja".

When a program in the build tools goes missing on Windows, the launcher now names it and asks you to restore it from your antivirus's quarantine or exclude the build tools folder from scanning, both while downloading the tools again and when a game build fails because of it. If files are missing right after the download, an alert asks you to check your antivirus and try again.

Play in Polish: choose Polski under Settings → Gameplay → Language. It's a community translation of the game's text; menus and pictures stay in English. New languages can now come with a launcher update alone.

Game updates now go in shorter folders, so on Windows a launcher kept in a deep folder no longer fails to build with "No such file or directory"; if the folder is still too deep, the launcher says so before building and suggests a shorter one such as C:\Games.

changes: Rumble can now be set stronger than the console's: light rumbles run the controller's motor more often, on any controller, including a GameCube controller on an adapter.

Nintendo's GameCube controller adapter, and copies of it in Wii U mode, now work on Windows without Zadig and on Linux, and play as on a GameCube: B and X are no longer swapped, FLUDD aims only once R clicks, and controllers rumble when the adapter's second plug is connected.
Fixed Super Mario Eclipse setup failing with "could not check out eclipse" on computers with their own git hooks set up, and the patching step now reports its progress.

A download of HD textures, a language pack or Super Mario Eclipse that stops partway is now deleted and started over once before trying the other download site, and an unfinished one left by an earlier try no longer counts against the free space setup needs.
The game plays any installed language pack, so new languages no longer need a game update.
Fixed Super Mario Eclipse failing to build when the launcher's folder has a comma in its path, such as "Recomps, Decomp and other ports".
With widescreen on, the map screen now fills the whole width, like the 16:9 map of later releases, instead of a 4:3 sheet with the level showing at both sides.
Fixed Pinna Park's climbing-cage mesh, and other HD fences and meshes, thinning out and vanishing a few metres from the camera with HD textures on.
With widescreen on, the blue screen that fades in when the camera goes inside a wall now covers the whole width, instead of only the 4:3 middle with hard edges at both sides.

launcher: Settings now has tabs down the side (Gameplay, Display, Graphics, Controls, Manage game, Saves and Launcher), so each setting is easier to find, and LB and RB switch between them.
Dark mode: Settings, the changelog and the launcher's other windows can be dark instead of light. Turn it on under Settings → Launcher.
Beta stays available under Settings → Launcher → Updates when the launcher can't load the list of update channels (offline, or GitHub's hourly limit); before, only Stable was offered.

Preparing the build tools on Windows now counts the files as it unpacks them, and stops with an explanation if unpacking makes no progress for five minutes, instead of staying on "Unpacking build tools…" for good.

Fixed the launcher never opening in the Steam Deck's Game Mode when it was added to Steam by hand without the --no-sandbox launch option: the Linux launcher now always starts with it, so Steam shortcuts work as they are.

On the Steam Deck, the first time you choose Play the launcher offers to add Super Mario Sunshine to Steam. Once it's in Steam, the Add to Steam banner shows a tick instead of disappearing, and selecting it updates the artwork or Skip Launcher.
Fixed updates failing to link your HD textures, HD cutscenes or Eclipse files into the new game version when an older update had left a broken link to a removed version ("EISDIR" on Windows).

Save states: Settings → Saves lists your save states with a picture of each and its Shines, blue coins, coins and lives, imports states others send you, and shows or deletes them. Settings → Controls has Save a state and Load the newest state, and a controller binding can be two buttons held together.

changes: Fixed the glove in the save state menu pointing away from the selected state instead of at it.
Fixed the stars missing with HD textures on when Mario bonks into a wall or stuns a Cataquack.

Fixed the circle wipes, like the one from the file select into Delfino Plaza and the one after you collect a Shine, showing a see-through striped grey instead of solid black at picture sharpness above Original (1×).
Fixed two sparkles from the GO! at the start of a level staying on screen for good, by the Shine counter and at the top right, after you pause and continue.
Fixed the character select's song playing through Eclipse's Shadow Mario episodes instead of the stage's music.
Fixed the coin counter's sparkle appearing to the right of the counter with screen icons at the edges.
Fixed Bloopers' punches often not hurting Mario at 60 and 120 fps.
Fixed some of Eclipse's secret courses, such as Daisy Cruiser's, having no music until Mario lost a life.
Fixed birds flying at half speed at 60 fps and a quarter speed at 120 fps.
Fixed the GO! letters being drawn far too big at 60 and 120 fps after the first one, as at the start of Eclipse's races.
Fixed a possible crash when Eclipse's Fire Petey breathes fire.
HD cutscene setup now names the movie and says the disc image is damaged or trimmed, instead of only "Expected THP 1.0 or 1.1".
Fixed F10 not showing the mouse cursor in borderless or fullscreen when it releases mouse look.
Fixed Eclipse getting slower the longer you played, until you restarted.
Fixed Shadow Mario's theme blaring for a moment at GO! in Eclipse's Shadow Mario episodes.
Fixed the goop bubbles drawing as opaque domes in flat colour quadrants (the Airstrip, worst in widescreen); they're translucent again.

Fixed the game using up all of the computer's memory within seconds of starting, before the title screen, when its shader cache had been damaged (for example by two games running at once); a damaged cache now starts over.
Hid the small grey placeholder cubes floating among the rail boards in Bianco Hills' secret course, The Secret of the Dirty Lake.
Fixed Borderless on some Windows PCs blanking the monitor at launch and every time you Alt-Tab back into the game, as exclusive fullscreen does.

Save states: in a level, L1 + R1 (LB + RB, or F5) saves the exact moment you're in. Pause and press them again to pick one from a list beside its picture, with its Shines and blue coins, and the game fades back to that moment, with everything where it was; the pause menu shows the buttons at its top right. F6 loads the newest. States are files you can share; one from another version of the game takes you to the same level and spot.
Building or updating the game no longer also makes sms-standalone, an extra 1.1 GB copy of the game with your disc inside that the launcher never used, so builds finish sooner and take less space.
Fixed the frame rate dropping during the wipe that opens and closes the map.

Fixed F10 not showing the mouse cursor in borderless or fullscreen when it releases mouse look.
Fixed Eclipse getting slower the longer you played, until you restarted.
Fixed Shadow Mario's theme blaring for a moment at GO! in Eclipse's Shadow Mario episodes.
Fixed the goop bubbles drawing as opaque domes in flat colour quadrants (the Airstrip, worst in widescreen); they're translucent again.

Fixed the frame rate dropping during the wipe that opens and closes the map.

launcher: Fixed the game failing to build on some Windows PCs with "The C compiler is not able to compile a simple test program", caused by the build losing the Windows system folders from its search path.
Play in French, German, Spanish or Italian: choose Language under Settings → Gameplay, and the launcher downloads that language's pack before the game starts.
Fixed the Spanish language pack failing to install on Windows PCs set to some non-English system languages, such as Russian, with "UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character".
Fixed the game build and HD texture setup crashing on some Windows PCs ("Access violation", or exit code 2816) when another Python install's settings were set on the PC.

Fixed every game update leaving the previous versions' files behind, which used several GB of disk space each. The launcher now keeps only the current and previous versions, and frees up the space from older ones the next time it opens.

Add to Steam is safer: it checks that all your other non-Steam games are still in Steam's list before saving it, never replaces its first backup of that list, and on Linux and the Steam Deck no longer restarts Steam itself, which could open Game Mode inside Desktop Mode.

Windows: advanced players can build with their own MSYS2 instead of the launcher's downloaded tools by setting the SMS_MSYS2_ROOT environment variable to its folder, for example on Windows 7 with the last MSYS2 that runs there.
Fixed setup files failing to download when you choose a drive root as the download location.

Fixed game setup failing on some older Windows setups with "fork: Resource temporarily unavailable" while preparing the game files, and game updates now reuse the previous version's decomp download instead of downloading it all again.

changes: Fixed Super Mario Eclipse's Delfino Plaza going almost black once you have more than 120 Shines.
Borderless on Windows is now a plain window covering the screen instead of a fullscreen mode, so it shouldn't blank the monitor as Exclusive fullscreen can.
Fixed the Dune Buds in Gelato Beach being silent: their filling and deflating sounds play again.
Fixed the water in Bowser's hot tub being invisible in the final fight. Bowser now sits in it, and the duck and Bowser Jr.'s boat float on it.
Fixed Super Mario Eclipse crashing on Mac when you leave a stage, and Eclipse's Yoshi colours now show on Mac too.
Fixed the picture breaking up into coloured blocks from the save select onward on some older Intel graphics at Original (1×) picture sharpness.

The game can be played in French, German, Spanish or Italian with a language pack, made from the European release: dialogue, cutscene subtitles, menus, the HUD, the title screen and the memory card screens.
Fixed accented letters such as á, ü and ñ in characters' speech bubbles in French, German, Spanish and Italian: a word like "más" no longer has its last letter dropped below the line.
Fixed the game crashing in Sirena Beach when the Phantamanta first splits into smaller mantas.

Fixed Super Mario Eclipse's ending movies losing their story when you skip them with A: skipping after the Bowser fight no longer leaves Delfino Plaza flooded with Shadow Mario back, and skipping the staff roll no longer loses its Shine.
Fixed Hotel Delfino's Boo blocks looking grey-blue and striped with HD textures on.
Fixed Luigi being unable to pick up nozzles from boxes in Super Mario Eclipse.

Fixed Super Mario Eclipse's music going missing after changing stages: secret courses' songs start with the course instead of after its intro, and stages such as Lacrima's hotel, Vaporware, Daisy Cruiser and Pizza Time play their music again.
Fixed Super Mario Eclipse crashing when you enter Red Lily's second episode.
Fixed Super Mario Eclipse crashing when you enter the Bowser fight that opens in Delfino Plaza after 239 Shines.
Fixed Super Mario Eclipse's Star Bits sometimes getting the wrong colour, and a memory error in its settings menu text that could crash the game.
A warp menu: open the debug overlay with the ` key, then press F8 or your controller's Back button to jump to any stage, episode or secret course, in the original game and in Super Mario Eclipse.

launcher: Start the game straight from Steam: add --play to the launcher's launch options and the game opens with your launcher settings, without the launcher's window. The launcher opens instead when the game needs setup or an update.
On Full HD Windows displays scaled above 125%, the launcher is sized as it is at 125% so it fits on screen.

Fixed the game failing to build on Macs whose newest macOS SDK is newer than their Command Line Tools can link ("ld: tapi error: malformed file"). The launcher now builds with the newest installed SDK that works.
You can now use the launcher with a game controller: move with the stick or d-pad, A selects, B goes back, Start opens Settings, and LB and RB switch between Settings, Controls and Manage game.

The portable Windows launcher always sets up in its SMS-Launcher-Portable folder without asking for a location, and the game's shader and HD texture caches now stay in that folder too instead of going to AppData.
Settings → Visuals has HD texture loading (Before each level, Whole pack, or While playing) and Prepare shaders ahead, to choose when the game loads HD textures and builds its shaders.

Add to Steam: a banner on the home screen, under the Discord one, adds the launcher to your Steam library as Super Mario Sunshine with artwork, for Big Picture and the Steam Deck. Turn on Skip Launcher when you add it and Steam starts the game straight away.
On Linux, launcher updates keep the AppImage's name and folder, so Steam shortcuts to it keep working. Re-add it to Steam once after this update.
Invert camera Y is now on by default for new players. Turn it off under Settings → Gameplay.

changes: Super Mario Eclipse now runs the code its v1.1.0 release ships, which removes the extra circle and blinking X button behind the FLUDD gauge in every stage.
Fixed Super Mario Eclipse crashing when you pick a character after unlocking Piantissimo.

Super Mario Eclipse's menus fill the widescreen frame properly, and its pause menu's Shine and blue coin counts are back on screen. Its own Aspect Ratio setting is hidden, since the game handles widescreen itself.
Fixed Super Mario Eclipse overwriting game memory at startup and while riding the green Yoshi.
Super Mario Eclipse's Delfino Plaza title card and pause menu no longer show "(null)" under the area's name.
The arrow under Super Mario Eclipse's B button balloon is red again instead of black.
Screen wipes, like the iris and warp transitions, run at their original speed at 60 and 120 fps, so warps no longer cut their sound short.
Fixed white specks on the sea with the High and Ultra graphics presets.
The goop Piranha Plant's hit voice plays once at 120 fps instead of twice.
The game ignores the keyboard and controllers while another window has focus, such as the launcher or another game, so they no longer move Mario in the background.

Entering a level no longer stutters the first time: the game builds the level's shaders and loads its HD textures into video memory while it loads, and HD textures no longer interrupt play while they finish in the background.
A cheat menu: press F9 in the game for God Mode, Infinite Lives, Infinite FLUDD, Movement Speed, Jump Height and Coin Multiplier.
Controllers rumble when the game rumbles. Turn it off with the Rumble option in the game's own options.
Fixed audio crackling and distortion after the game slows down or hitches.

launcher: If you already have HD textures, the launcher downloads the new HD texture extras on their own (about 65 MB) instead of the whole pack, and again whenever a newer set comes out.
Show on Discord: while you play, your Discord profile shows where you are in the game, your Shine count and how long you've played. Turn it off under Manage game.
The launcher keeps its size on Windows displays with high scaling.
A changelog: see what changed in the launcher and the game with the new button beside Settings. It opens by itself once after an update.
"Skip intro movies" is now "Skip cutscenes", since it skips every movie.
With Super Mario Eclipse turned on in Settings, the home screen shows Eclipse artwork and notes that the launcher isn't affiliated with the Eclipse team.

changes: HD textures cover 208 more textures the UHD pack lacked, including the Pianta and balloon counters, the pause screen's maps, menus and Peach.
Heavy scenes like Delfino Plaza run much smoother: the game takes less than half as long on each frame.
Wiggler's music speeds up when you hit him and powers down when he's defeated, as on the GameCube.
Petey Piranha, Mecha Bowser and other bosses animate at their original speed at 60 and 120 fps.
The episode select screen shows its coloured background again instead of black.
Fixed dark fog bands and shimmering HD textures under the sea in Noki Bay.
Fixed Shadow Mario never taking Peach in Super Mario Eclipse's Delfino Plaza.
Portal movies keep playing when Skip cutscenes is on.
The game reports what you're doing for Discord.
Super Mario Eclipse downloads from SMS Launcher's own mirror, with GameBanana as the fallback.
Fixed Super Mario Eclipse crashing when you enter Bianco Hills or Erto Rock.
Fixed the camera staying tilted in Super Mario Eclipse after Delfino Plaza's opening cutscene plays to the end.

launcher: HDR settings for Windows: calibration, paper white, peak brightness, contrast, saturation and highlights.
FSR 1 and NIS upscaling under Settings → Picture → Scaling, with a quality choice.
The top bar shows how many players are online. Turn off anonymous usage sharing any time under Manage game.

changes: HDR output on Windows, and on more graphics cards.
NIS (NVIDIA Image Scaling) joins FSR 1 as an upscaler.
Fixed the Eclipse crashes at every stage exit and in the Tutorial on Windows.
Fixed Puffer self-collisions when firing at Petey at high frame rates.
Held sound effects, like the Rocket nozzle charge, keep playing at 60 fps.
Button prompt glyphs draw correctly with the system font.

launcher: Graphics presets: Low, Medium, High, Ultra and Steam Deck.
Button prompts: Original, Xbox, PlayStation 5, Steam Deck, keyboard, or Automatic.
A game source row with only a branch, tag or commit now uses our fork.

changes: Button prompts for Xbox, PlayStation, Steam Deck and keyboard.
Smoother heavy scenes: less time spent in the vertex loader and thread switches.
A full crash report is written on every platform.
Fixed the Turbo nozzle writing past its own memory.

launcher: Controller button remapping on the Controls page, plus Soft L and Soft R bindings.
The activity log now docks inside the launcher, and Copy log copies the full run.
A check-for-updates button next to the launcher update status.
A Heat-wave effect switch under Settings → Picture.
A note for SteamOS and Steam Deck players about Steam Input.

changes: 60 and 120 fps gameplay stays at full speed when the display makes the game wait.
GameCube controller adapters are supported.
Controller buttons can be remapped.
Native crashes now log their code and location.
Fixed Mario's flags in Super Mario Eclipse.
Fixed the Gelato gatekeeper's goop angles.
Linux builds use the system graphics driver's own libraries.
The performance overlay costs less to draw.
